historical_references.reference: Houshang is a Persian name, which appears in various forms in Islamic sources. It is believed to have originated from the Old Persian word 'hushang', meaning 'good news' or 'auspicious'. One historical reference is found in the works of the Persian historian Ibn al-Athir (1260-1316 CE). He mentions a certain Houshang ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi, who was a vizier (adviser) to the Seljuq Sultan Sanjar (1118-1157 CE). This Houshang is known to have played a significant role in diplomacy and negotiations during the Seljuq Empire's conflicts with the Crusaders and the Byzantines.

Another historical reference to the name Houshang can be found in the works of the Persian historian Al-Maqdisi (946-1000 CE). He mentions a certain Houshang ibn Chilchil, who was a governor of Tabaristán (northern Iran) during the Buyid Empire (932-1055 CE). This Houshang is known to have led successful military campaigns against the Qarmathians (an Islamic sect) and the Turkish tribes in the region.
